preconditions: Select the operation explicitly: tail/read, append, follow, clear or export.
Use JSON-compatible, sanitized event fields and a project/output path within the current task scope.
Treat rotation, partial logs and duplicated follower events as possible; this is not a durable exactly-once event bus.
The export helpers may require optional pandas/Parquet dependencies; developer load-test utilities are outside this declaration.

expected_effects.effect: Append a timestamped row and create .botte if needed; an existing large log may first be reduced to its newest half.
expected_effects.scope: The selected project .botte/events.jsonl and its retained history.
expected_effects.basis: events.log_event serializes before mutation, calls _maybe_rotate and then appends; ordinary path/serialization failures are best-effort.
expected_effects.impact: Makes decisions visible; consumes storage and can remove older history on rotation. A single large append can exceed the rotation threshold.
expected_effects.verification: Append sanitized fixture rows and read them back; force a small threshold and check which history remains.

expected_effects.effect: Read or follow retained rows, omitting malformed JSON lines; follow polls repeatedly until its caller stops.
expected_effects.scope: Local event file, CPU/I/O, caller output and any stdout capture.
expected_effects.basis: read_events reads the current file; follow_events polls and resets its position when the retained file shrinks.
expected_effects.impact: Enables debugging and replay; reads can expose supplied metadata and following may repeat retained rows after rotation.
expected_effects.verification: Use fixture logs with a malformed line and a rotation, then inspect emitted rows without triggering external actions.

expected_effects.effect: Delete the log when clear is requested, or create/overwrite an export output when an export helper is invoked.
expected_effects.scope: The project log or the explicit/derived CSV/Parquet output path.
expected_effects.basis: clear_events unlinks the log; export helpers write their output. CSV projects selected fields and shortens reason text.
expected_effects.impact: Clearing removes local evidence; exports can preserve or disclose private fields and are not always lossless or reversible.
expected_effects.verification: Use a copied fixture, check the distinct output path before export, compare retained fields and verify clear only targets that fixture.

downstream_effects.effect: Dashboards, replay tools or external consumers may draw conclusions or initiate actions from retained events.
downstream_effects.scope: Consumers of the local log and any exported copies.
downstream_effects.basis: The logger supplies caller-provided observations; it does not attest to external action completion or control consumers.
downstream_effects.impact: Missing, duplicate or rotated rows can distort counts or lead a consumer to repeat work.
downstream_effects.verification: Reconcile event identifiers and independent task evidence before making a state-changing decision.

reversibility.strategy: Ordinary appends can be superseded by a correcting observation. Restore cleared/rotated history only from an existing authorized backup; handle exported copies separately.
residual_effects: Removed history cannot be reconstructed from the remaining log alone.
Exports and disclosures to consumers are not recalled by deleting the local log.

retry.check_before_retry: Check whether an append already exists and whether rotation occurred. Repeated appends have new timestamps; readers/followers are not exactly-once acknowledgments.
retry.stop_condition: Stop repeated writes on the same unresolved path/serialization error; never infer permission to repeat the underlying action from an absent log row.

required_scope: Existing task authorization for reading or mutating the selected project log, and separately for clearing history or writing/sharing exports.

analysis.summary: The event log is a useful local observation channel with explicit loss, retention and retry limits. It provides no durability receipt, action proof or automatic privacy guarantee.
uncertainties: Persistence is best-effort; caller success does not establish that an event is present.
Concurrent append/rotation and follower replay are not transactional.
Event payloads and export destinations are supplied by callers and may contain identifying data.

reuse.target: Use retained decisions to investigate routing behavior or declaration coverage.
reuse.rationale: Timestamped operation records provide context for comparing what a caller intended with what it reported.
adaptations: Account for retention windows, duplicate rows and missing events.
Keep detailed outcome evidence in the task report; sanitize any shared extract.
reuse.validation: Compare known fixture actions with a log containing a duplicate, a malformed row and rotated history; report uncertainty instead of treating the log as complete.
